title: allow parallel/multithreaded/multipart transfers between remotes
body:
#### What is your current rclone version (output from `rclone version`)?
v1.63.0

#### What problem are you are trying to solve?
Specifically, transfers from S3 to S3 are much slower than they have to be. In our case, the buckets need different credentials, so remote copying is not an option (however, in our experience remote copy is actually *slower* than local copy, and it is also not done in parallel). This happens sequentially, resulting for us in speeds of about 70MiB/s. With multithreading we can download at speeds limited only by disk and network speed. Same thing for upload using multipart.
So, actually, download to local and re-uploading is faster than a direct copy, but still half the speed we should have; AND requires more fumbling with infrastructure as the disk needs to be big enough for holding the files (> TiB).

I would like to make the in-memory copy limited only by network (and maybe cpu/mem). Our main problem is S3, but I think the solution should be at least somewhat generic.

See related forum post: https://<redacted-host>/t/s3-s3-large-file-copy/18574/4


#### How do you think rclone should be changed to solve that?

I would actually be happy to receive some opinions on how to go about it ;-)

My initial though would be to change (or create a new) the multithreaded downloading to make it more similiar to how multipart uploads work. Instead of simply selecting threads and then using `filesize/threads` to get ranges AND threads,  we would us `chunk-size` for ranges and `download-concurrency` for number of threads.

Then we could plug this into the multi-part uploading by selecting the same sizes.

But I'm fuzzy on the details, and on how to make it more generic.

Is this a feasible idea? Any other approaches that might be better than the one I suggested?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Now that we've merged the first part of this - thank you @participant3 and @reporter I've had a go at the next part.

This is making the multipart upload generic.

I'd really appreciate testing on this.

[v1.64.0-beta.7247.5bd9e6527.multithread](https://<redacted-host>/branch/multithread/v1.64.0-beta.7247.5bd9e6527.multithread/) on branch [multithread](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/multithread) (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

The main changes I've made are:

- pool the memory use - this is really important for not exploding memory use
- factor a multipart uploader to lib/multipart from backend/s3
- tidy and polish the ChunkWriter code
- don't do buffering when writing to local disk

This takes all the memory management out of the s3 backend which is what I wanted to achieve - that will also fix #7141

I'd appreciate it if you would test and/or review this branch.

I want to implement ChunkWriter in the following backends for v1.64 when we are sure that the interface is good.

- `azureblob`
- `b2`
- `box`
- `gcs`
- `oracleobjectstorage` ( @participant5 maybe you'd like to help with this? )

Other possibilities

- `chunker` (see #5041)
- `dropbox` (currently not parallel uploading but there is an interface)

Still to do:

- I note also that we probably need to implement this in some of the Overlay file systems (eg `combine`, `union`) - the integration tests are failing at the moment because of the missing implementations.
- Accounting is still broken!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I've merged all the outstanding multithread code to master now :-)

I had a [question on the forum](https://<redacted-host>/t/improve-transfer-stats-calculation-for-multipart-uploads/41172/3) about this

> How is --multi-thread-streams different from --s3-upload-concurrency?

That is a good question and one I'm going to have to explain in the docs. Maybe the options need simplifying here.

Here is what has happened

### Old rclone

- if size below `--s3-upload-cutoff`  (default 200M) do single part upload
- otherwise do multipart upload using `--s3-concurrency` to set the concurrency used by the uploader.

### New rclone

- if size below `--s3-upload-cutoff` (default 200M) do single part upload
- if size below `--multi-thread-cutoff` (default 256M) do multipart upload using `--s3-concurrency` to set the concurrency used by the uploader.
- otherwise do multipart upload using  `--multi-thread-streams` to set the concurrency

Now that I've written that out it looks needlessly confusing.

I guess the options for rationalising it are

1. use `--s3-concurrency` instead of `--multi-thread-streams` to set the concurrency. This means each backend can set different concurrency levels.
- this is backwards compatible with people's config
- it means `--multi-thread-streams` will no longer be used (or maybe the default for backends that don't care)
- this will require changing the `ChunkWriter` interface to return the desired concurrency along with the desired chunk size
2. use `--multi-thread-streams` to set the concurrency everywhere. Neat, but doesn't allow different concurrency settings for different backends.
- this is not backwards compatible with people's config
- this will require reading the value of `--multi-thread-streams` in the backend (easy)
3. use a hybrid - use the maximum of `--s3-concurrency` and `--multi-thread-streams` - this allows individual control for each backend but has a global override
- this is backwards compatible with people's config
- it means `--multi-thread-streams` still does something useful
- this will require changing the `ChunkWriter` interface

Any thoughts?

PS I've pushed the 1.64 milestone back 2 weeks to allow a bit more time for this feature to settle!

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I noticed the [top Google result](https://<redacted-host>/t/s3-concurrency-multi-thread-streams-vs-s3-upload-concurrency/34191) for "rclone s3 concurrency" is confusion about `--multi-thread-streams` vs `--s3-concurrency`, so the single flag may be easier from a user perspective.

What scenarios would benefit from backend-specific flags? Maybe there's a case where we can read chunks from one backend faster than we can write to another, so we want to have lower read concurrency vs write concurrency? (This feels unlikely - rclone will always buffer the diff in speeds. Unless there's a remote with a lower RPS limit with higher per-chunk throughput than the second remote...) Or maybe there are scenarios with `combine` setups that would benefit from this?

If there's not a good reason for backend-specific concurrency, then it seems like this could be made much simpler by moving to `--multi-thread-streams`, and deprecate `--s3-concurrency`. We don't have to break people's configs though - we could alias `--s3-concurrency` to `--multi-thread-streams`, and print a warning about the deprecation. If the user has both, I'd say go with the higher value (and maybe include that in the warning message.) Same could be done for `--s3-upload-cutoff`. This is basically option 3 that you mentioned, but I think we should probably push users to `--multi-thread-streams` to reduce confusion.

The one downside to the unified `--multi-thread-streams` flag is that it's not clear which backends it applies to. When looking for flags compatible with a backend, I typically do something like `rclone help flags|grep s3`. So maybe we could improve communication/docs for what remotes this flag affects.

From the docs

### --multi-thread-streams=N ###

When using multi thread transfers (see above `--multi-thread-cutoff`)
this sets the number of streams to use. Set to `0` to disable multi
thread transfers (Default 4).

If the backend has a `--backend-upload-concurrency` setting (eg
`--s3-upload-concurrency`) then this setting will be used as the
number of transfers instead if it is larger than the value of
`--multi-thread-streams` or `--multi-thread-streams` isn't set.

@participant7
> I haven't read the details of the implementation yet but can you confirm that #6179 should be rewritten to use the new `ChunkWriter` abstraction?

Only if the chunks can be uploaded in parallel and in any order. I think this is the case! The performance gains only start to show when rclone isn't filling the upload network pipe and that requires a very fast source and a big upload pipe. For your average SSD to average upload I don't think you'll notice much speed difference.


> Also, is the current issue (#7056) a duplicate of #4798?

Yes it looks like it! I'll close that issue now.
